It checks that click.echo (and things built on it, e.g. click.termui / _termui_impl pager or prompt output) behaves correctly when sys.stdout / sys.stderr are None (e.g. running under pythonw on Windows, or a GUI app with no console streams). Currently click probably crashes with AttributeError/TypeError when sys.stdout is None, because the text/binary stream wrappers in src/click/_compat.py assume a real stream (e.g. _default_text_stdout / _wrap_io_open / _find_binary_writer / _force_correct_text_writer / isatty / strip_ansi / auto_wrap_for_ansi), and src/click/utils.py echo() calls into them, and src/click/_termui_impl.py also touches sys.stdout/sys.stdin directly.

   cd /click && python -c "
import sys, click
sys.stdout = None
sys.stderr = None
click.echo('hello')
click.echo('err', err=True)

"
